e1: 129は救急医療支援センター。救急費用で治療を断られたり退院を拒否されたときに連絡。
経済的理由で適切な救急を拒否されてはいけません。129で国の先払い手続きを案内。
緊急時はまず119で搬送・救助。病院で費用問題なら129。
e2: 119は火災・救急・救助を統合処理する韓国の代表緊急番号。
「どこで・何が・何人」を順に伝える。煙なら低姿勢避難後に通報。
e3: 112は警察緊急通報。進行中の犯罪、脅迫、交通事故、家庭内暴力など。
話せないときは112 SMS通報可。位置情報を許可すると出動が早い。
e4: 1339 is the health call center for after-hours ERs and 24-hour pharmacies.
Useful when you need a hospital you can reach now. Give area and symptoms for nearby options; infectious disease guidance is also available.
e5: 1577-2584 is the Crime Victim Support Center—medical, counseling, and legal referrals after violence or robbery.
This is public recovery support separate from investigation—contact early rather than coping alone.
e6: 02-3210-0404 is the MOFA consular call center—24/7 Korean help for citizens abroad.
For passport loss, arrest, accidents, or disasters overseas, contact local police/hospital first, then call. From abroad: +82-2-3210-0404.
e7: 109 is the 24/7 anonymous mental health crisis line.
You do not have to face severe anxiety, depression, or isolation alone. Counselors listen without judgment and can link local mental health or emergency services.
e8: 111 is the NIS reporting line for espionage, terror, North Korea-linked threats, and national security concerns.
Industrial technology leaks and counter-intelligence tips are included. Overlap with police 113—either line is fine.
e9: 113 is police counter-espionage—for espionage, tech leaks, terror, and suspected spy activity.
If you see suspicious approaches or theft attempts, note time, place, and behavior when reporting.
e10: 1338 is integrated civil defense reporting—for drones, unknown vessels, suspicious military activity, and similar signs.
Record time and location if safe; evacuate first if there is danger.
e11: 1337 reports military secrets, military espionage, and defense-industry spying (Military Security Support Command).
Use for suspected leaks of military or defense technology; ordinary crimes go to 112.
e12: 122 is Korea Coast Guard emergency—for distress, accidents, illegal fishing, and marine pollution.
At sea, tidal flats, or islands, remember 122 with 119. Give precise location (island name, coordinates, buoys).
e13: 1393 is the suicide prevention hotline—24/7 when you or someone nearby is at risk.
Can be used with 109. If life is in immediate danger, call 119 or 112 first.
e14: 128 handles environmental pollution complaints—odors, illegal dumping, water and air pollution.
State when, where, and what type of pollution to speed site checks.
e15: 1399 is food safety counseling—for food poisoning, bad products, and mislabeled goods.
Have product name, store, expiry, and photos ready when reporting.
c1: 1588-2504 is KEX public tow on expressways—call before private tow to avoid overcharges after breakdowns or crashes.
Free distance may apply; use this first when confused right after an incident.
c2: 1588-2100 is expressway emergency tow to move vehicles from shoulders to safety.
Stopping on the highway is high risk—use hazards and a triangle, then call this, 119, or 112 as needed.
c3: 112 can verify a traffic accident on scene—official record of investigation, alcohol tests, and statements.
Reporting right after a crash helps insurance and disputes; if injured, call 119 first.
c4: If anyone may be hurt after a crash, call 119 for an ambulance—even mild pain can worsen later.
c5: 1566-8000 is a major insurers’ accident line for roadside help, tow, and rental car links.
Save your own insurer’s number too; on expressways prefer public tow (1588-2504).
c6: 1544-0119 guides injury claims when the other driver is uninsured or flees.
c7: 110 connects post-accident admin needs—fines, license, and civil complaints through the government helpline.
c8: 182 helps find lost items on buses and subways and guides missing-person services.
Prepare time, route, seat, and item details; missing children/adults can also be reported here.
c9: 1544-7788 is Korail—trains, seats, lost items, and delay compensation.
For items lost on a train, give the train number, station where you got off, and time.
h1: 1588-1300 updates bank, card, insurance, and telecom addresses in one request after a move.
Apply within 1–2 weeks of moving to reduce missed mail and notices.
h2: 1661-2642 is the neighbor noise mediation center with on-site mediators.
Use when the building office cannot resolve conflict; logs and recordings help.
h3: 1566-9009 HUG center checks registry and rights before jeonse contracts to prevent deposit fraud.
Consult before sending deposit; urgent-only deals or agent-only meetings are red flags.
h4: 1670-1004 is city gas emergency—24/7 for smell or leaks.
Do not touch switches; ventilate, evacuate, then report. Follow local gas company guidance.
h5: 123 is KEPCO for outages, line problems, and shock or fire risk from electricity.
Electrocution or fire risk: 119 first; simple outages: 123.
h6: 1577-0600 is K-water for water, dams, quality, and some outage/leak guidance.
City water leaks may be faster via local 120; if unsure, 110 can route you.
h7: 131 is KMA weather—for typhoon, flood, heat, cold alerts and daily forecasts.
Check before hiking, boating, or outdoor plans.
l1: 132 Legal Aid offers free lawyer consults and litigation support by income.
Before suing on traffic, lease, labor, or family issues, 132 helps set direction cost-effectively.
l2: 1577-1000 NHIS-related line—for out-of-pocket cap refunds and similar.
Ask if you paid heavily in a year without refund notice.
l3: 1332 FSS consumer protection—for voice phishing, illegal loans, and financial product harm.
Bank, insurance, card, and investment complaints accepted; if rushed to transfer, call 1398 first.
l4: 1398 is dedicated voice-phishing reporting—hang up on fake prosecutors/police/regulators and call immediately.
You can report during the call; before transferring money is the critical window.
l5: 1811-9000 personal data breach center—leaks, unauthorized collection, deletion and blocking steps.
ID/account leaks and marketing without consent count; for hacking/ransomware also use 118.
l6: 1544-0990 Consumer Agency mediates refund and contract disputes for free—bring contract, payment, and chat records.
l7: 126 National Tax Service—for income/VAT filing, notices, refunds, and Hometax questions.
l8: 1661-7600 local tax line—for vehicle, property, and local income tax.
l9: 118 is KISA cyber security—for hacking, ransomware, phishing sites, and illegal spam.
Voice phishing: 1398; personal data: 1811-9000; money fraud: 112 and 1332.
l10: 1301 Prosecution Service—for drugs, public corruption, and special investigation tips.
For theft or assault needing immediate police, use 112.
l11: 1372 Fair Trade Commission—for collusion, unfair terms, ads, franchise and distribution issues.
Individual refund fights are often better at Consumer Agency 1544-0990.
l12: 1600-5500 Credit Counseling & Recovery—for arrears, debt adjustment, and personal rehabilitation links.
With multiple debts, try public counseling before illegal lenders.
l13: 1397 MFC policy finance—including Sunshine loans and financial counseling.
Check eligibility before high-interest emergency loans.
l14: 1331 National Human Rights Commission—for discrimination and human rights complaints and procedures.
f1: 1661-2129 senior care counseling—welfare checks and visit care links for seniors living alone.
Local services may also route via municipal 120 or 110.
f2: 117 school violence reporting by phone or text—consider public report alongside school steps to protect students.
f3: 1366 women’s emergency line—24/7 for domestic/sexual violence and stalking; shelter links.
If in immediate danger, also call 112; counseling is confidential.
f4: 1899-0088 digital sex crime victim support—illegal filming takedown and investigation/counseling links.
Do not destroy evidence; follow guidance for deletion and investigation together.
f5: 1345 immigration help center—visa, stay, and daily life in multiple languages; useful for foreign family and friends.
f6: 1388 youth counseling—anonymous help with school, family, friends, and career; crisis links to 109 and 1393.
f7: 1355 National Pension Service—pension receipt, enrollment, contributions, and estimates.
f8: 1389 elder abuse reporting—physical, emotional, financial abuse and neglect.
f9: 182 also guides missing children and missing persons—report quickly after disappearance.
Prepare recent photos, clothing, and last seen location; clear danger also warrants 112.
w1: 1350 MOEL helpline—unemployment benefits, employment aid, contracts, and wage arrears.
Unpaid wages and unfair dismissal procedures can be explained here.
w2: 1588-0075 KCOMWEL—industrial accidents, employment insurance, and vocational rehab.
After a workplace injury, ask about filing deadlines and documents.
w3: 1644-8000 training and “Tomorrow Learning Card” counseling for job change and certifications.
w4: 1544-4140 equal employment counseling—workplace harassment, discrimination, and relief steps.
Use when internal reporting is hard or retaliation is a concern.
g1: 110 government civil helpline routes central, local, and public agency services nationwide—call when unsure who to contact.
g2: 02-120 Seoul Dasan Call Center—Seoul life, transport, and environment services; reachable from outside Seoul on mobile.
g3: 1588-2188 Gov24 call center—resident registration, family relations certificates, and digital ID issuance.
g4: 031-120 Gyeonggi Province call center handles local administration and daily civil services for residents.
g5: 032-120 Incheon call center handles local administration and daily civil services for residents.

g14: 041-120 South Chungcheong call center handles local administration and daily civil services for residents.

g20: 125 Customs—cross-border shopping clearance, duties, prohibited items, and declarations.
If held at customs, have tracking number and item description ready.
g21: 1588-9090 Military Manpower Administration—conscription, enlistment, discharge, and duty questions.
